index.title: Verify any document. Issue any credential. Bridge any PKI.
index.lead: Identity infrastructure built on W3C and IETF standards. Technologically neutral — works with any stack, any vendor, any government. Open source reference implementations anyone can deploy.
index.uc_title: Identity infrastructure for the real world
index.uc_desc: Each use case below is either live or in active development, using open standards for identity resolution and credential verification.
index.surf_desc: Four surfaces, progressive adoption. Start with zero friction in the browser, go deeper as you need.
index.std_desc: Two DID methods, both on the W3C standards track, both with live resolvers. They bridge existing trust infrastructure into the DID ecosystem without replacing anything.
index.source_desc: We publish reference implementations for every standard we propose. Traditional vendors can adopt the standards without using our code. Or fork it. Apache 2.0.
index.p_sovereignty_short: Your keys, your device, your data.
index.p_nolock_short: Fork it, export it, migrate freely.
index.p_transparency_short: Open source, open governance, open audit.
index.p_neutrality_short: You choose the technology, not us.

why.title: Your identity. Your proof.
why.lead: Why we built open infrastructure for sovereign identity — and why it matters that no one owns it.
why.s1_title: Identity is something someone else confirms
why.s1_p1: In most of the world, proving who you are means carrying a physical card, presenting it to an institution, hoping they believe it, and trusting that whoever holds your data won't misuse it.
why.s1_p2: Your identity exists only when someone else says it does. A government office. A bank. A platform. If they lose your record, revoke your access, or simply close for the day — you stop being provable.
why.s1_p3: This isn't a technology problem. It's a design choice. And it can be redesigned.
why.s2_title: When identity depends on someone else
why.s2_p3: These aren't hypothetical. They're happening now, in the countries where we live and build.
why.s3_title: Identity doesn't have to be a favor
why.s3_p1: Identity can be a mathematical proof you carry yourself. W3C Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials make this technically possible. A cryptographic key pair on your device. A credential signed by an authority you choose to trust. A proof you present without revealing more than you must.
why.s3_p2: The technology exists. What didn't exist — until now — was open infrastructure to make it deployable. Not a product. Not a platform. Public infrastructure, like roads or the postal service. Anyone can use it, anyone can verify it, anyone can fork it.
why.s4_p1: Existing authorities (governments, professional bodies, universities) issue verifiable credentials signed with their own keys. We don't replace them. We give them a standards-based channel to issue digitally what they already issue on paper.
why.s4_p2: A peer-to-peer network where every node can verify credentials independently, offline, without calling a central server. The credential holder controls what they share and with whom.
why.s4_p3: Cryptographic timestamps on a public ledger prove that a credential existed at a specific time. Not the content — just the proof that it was issued. Immutable, auditable, independent of Attestto.
why.s4_p4: Every component is open source (Apache 2.0). Every standard is W3C or IETF. Any government can fork the entire stack and never depend on us. That's the point.
why.s5_p1: Infrastructure earns trust by what it refuses to do, not by what it promises. These aren't marketing principles. They're constraints we enforce in code.

standards.hero_title: Open DID methods for real-world identity
standards.hero_p1: Attestto develops and maintains two Decentralized Identifier methods — both on the W3C standards track, both with live resolvers, both open source.
standards.hero_p2: These methods bridge existing trust infrastructure (national PKIs, domain name systems) into the DID ecosystem without replacing anything. Verifiers get interoperable resolution. Issuers keep their existing keys.

downloads.hero_lead: All Attestto apps and tools in one place. Desktop, mobile, browser extension, web apps, and SDKs for developers.
downloads.apps_desc: Install Station on your desktop for verification, signing, and mesh networking. Open the App on your phone for credentials and exams. Every surface connects to the same identity.
downloads.station_desc: Your verification station. Encrypted vault, document OCR, national digital signature support, trust store. Required for mesh network nodes and professional modules (notarial, medical, legal). macOS, Windows, and Linux.
downloads.station_note: v0.1.0 — Changelog · Requires macOS 12+, Windows 10+, or Ubuntu 20.04+
downloads.extension_desc: Browser extension that validates document signatures client-side and manages your decentralized identity on the web.
downloads.extension_note: Coming soon to Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons. Available from source code.
downloads.web_desc: Verify and sign documents directly from your browser. No installation, no registration.
downloads.verify_desc: Verify signed documents. Drop a PDF and check the cryptographic signature, chain of trust, and document integrity. Supports national PKI roots per jurisdiction.
downloads.sign_desc: Sign documents with your verified identity. Simple electronic signature, advanced signature with Attestto CA, or Costa Rican Digital Signature.
downloads.platform_desc: Complete dashboard for organizations. KYC/KYB, credentials, treasury, data vault, and more.
downloads.dev_desc: Integrate credential verification, decentralized identity, and verifiable schemas in your application. Everything is open source on GitHub.
downloads.community_desc: Attestto is open source. Report bugs, propose features, contribute code, or just follow along.
downloads.community_github_desc: Source code, issues, pull requests, and releases from all repositories.
downloads.community_contact_desc: For institutions, governments, and partners who want to board the Ark.
downloads.community_arch_desc: Learn the full architecture: Station, Wallet, Mesh, Ceremony, and Trust.

ark.appliance_desc: A clean Linux laptop boots from live USB. No hard drive, no history, no external network. The ceremony software creates a private WiFi mesh to distribute Shamir shares to shareholder devices.
ark.arch_desc: The connection between desktop and mobile is direct over local WiFi. No intermediary servers, no cloud, no internet dependency.
ark.arch_note: Privacy is not a policy — it is a mathematical guarantee.
ark.br_desc: CPF, CNH, digital RG. Integration with ICP-Brasil and gov.br.
ark.cer_desc: The CA key generation ceremony occurs in a completely isolated environment. No internet connection. The only network is an encrypted local mesh between shareholder devices.
ark.ceremony_desc: Sovereign appliance for CA key ceremonies. Air-gapped Linux laptop, Shamir share distribution via local mesh.
ark.ceremony_l2: Key is split, original is destroyed
ark.comp_desc: Start with one component and grow into the full architecture. Onboard progressively — deploy Station today, add Wallet tomorrow, join the Mesh when ready. Every step adds value, and the full architecture is greater than the sum of its parts.
ark.countries_desc: Each country gets its own Certificate Authority, its own key ceremony, and its own governance. Each runs as an independent sovereign root anchored on a public ledger of its choice.
ark.cr_desc: Identity card, driver's license, ROS. Designed to integrate with national census, payment infrastructure, and digital signature frameworks.
ark.cta_desc: If any of the roles above fits you, write to us. We are looking for the institutions, professionals, and developers who want to help build sovereign digital identity in the open.
ark.gov_desc: The Certificate Authority private key is designed to be split using Shamir's Secret Sharing. The architecture ensures no individual actor — including Attestto — can sign unilaterally.
ark.hero_ext_desc: Log in to any website with no username and no password, and sign documents with one click — your data stays private, your accounts stay yours.
ark.hero_mesh_desc: Stations, extensions, and mobile apps can join a shared, encrypted network — your data lives across the community, not on a single server.
ark.hero_station_desc: Verify, sign, and safeguard your documents — all on your own computer. Nothing leaves your device unless you decide.
ark.how_desc: Desktop and phone work together over local WiFi. Images and biometric data never leave your network — the connection is direct, no servers or cloud.
ark.lead: The infrastructure for issuing, verifying, and governing verifiable credentials — open source, sovereign by design, and built so any institution can participate in the trust root. No single point of failure, no single point of control.
ark.mesh_desc: Encrypted P2P network over libp2p. State synchronization between local devices and national nodes without a central server.
ark.mesh_l1: Blind Courier principle — nodes can't read the data they carry
ark.mesh_l4: Cryptographic anchoring on a public ledger
ark.multi_desc: Each country has its own electronic signature scheme. The appliance supports PKCS#11 to integrate with local signing hardware.
ark.mx_desc: INE, CURP, federal license. Integration with e.firma SAT.
ark.onchain_desc: The CA public key is anchored on a public ledger (Solana today, chain-agnostic by design). The architecture anchors every certificate event on-chain (planned via the on-chain attestation pipeline) — auditable by anyone, at any time. Each jurisdiction can choose its anchoring layer.
ark.persona1_desc: National regulators and public institutions. Evaluate the architecture, request a briefing, and explore institutional participation.
ark.persona2_desc: If you live with the "signature validity unknown" red banner every day, Station is built for you. Verify CR-signed PDFs natively.
ark.persona3_desc: Run a pilot on a real onboarding or signing flow. Issue verifiable credentials your counterparties can verify offline.
ark.persona4_desc: Every component is open source. Read the code, file issues, ship a module, fork a country deployment.
ark.persona5_desc: Stand up a sovereign CA in your jurisdiction with your own shareholders and your own ceremony. The architecture is one-per-country by design.
ark.rights_desc: Identity, signing, anchoring, recovery, and verification are citizen rights — not services. They are free forever for every person Ark reaches, in every country it serves. Commerce funds the network so citizens never have to. No premium tiers. No paywalls. No exceptions.
ark.shareholders_desc: Phase 1A is founder-only with all shares held by Attestto. Institutional shareholder positions are reserved for Phase 1B once formal partners join. Each share alone is useless — only when the threshold gathers can the key be temporarily reconstructed.
ark.sss_desc: The CA Ed25519 key is generated in an air-gapped ceremony and split into N shares. A threshold K is required to reconstruct it. The original key is destroyed after the split.
ark.station_desc: Electron desktop application. Your verification station, credential vault, and mesh network node.
ark.station_l1: Document verification with OCR and census
ark.station_l2: Encrypted local vault with xsalsa20-poly1305 + scrypt
ark.station_l3: Electronic signature today; smartcard Digital Signature (PKCS#11) planned
ark.station_l4: Every installation can join the mesh as a node
ark.step1_desc: Select the document type to verify. Station generates a unique session QR code.
ark.step2_desc: The QR opens the mobile app with the WebSocket connection preconfigured. Your phone connects directly to your desktop.
ark.step2_title: Scan the QR with your phone
ark.step3_desc: Front, back of document, and selfie with liveness proof (blink detection). Everything transmits in real-time to the desktop.
ark.step4_desc: Station runs OCR, extracts MRZ data, validates the document, and generates the verifiable credential.
ark.step5_desc: The credential is stored encrypted in the local vault. Sign it with Digital Signature, anchor it on a public ledger, or share it via verifiable presentation.
ark.tls1_desc: The Attestto ID extension validates certificates client-side against vault.attestto.sol and surfaces a sovereignty trust score in the browser. Day-1 deployment, no DNS infrastructure changes.
ark.tls2_desc: Publish TLSA records in DNS pointing to Attestto CA certificates. Requires the domain to use DNSSEC. DANE validators already exist in some browsers.
ark.tls3_desc: A bridging service that lets sites cross-publish their Attestto-issued certificate alongside a globally-trusted certificate, so browsers without DANE or the extension still see a valid chain while the sovereign certificate is recognized by participating clients.
ark.tls4_desc: Participate in standards working groups so browsers natively recognize CA roots anchored in decentralized registries (blockchain, IPNS, SNS).
ark.tls_desc: The ultimate goal: TLS certificates issued by Attestto CA recognized natively by browsers. Four parallel paths, each with a different time horizon.
ark.tls_title: Four paths to the sovereign web
ark.trust_desc: CA trust framework with Shamir shareholders, on-chain transparency, and governance distributed across institutions.
ark.trust_l1: CA key split: 2-of-3 today, extensible to 3-of-5 with institutional partners
ark.types_desc: The system supports different ceremonies according to the CA lifecycle.
ark.vlei_desc: The framework requires each shareholder to hold a verified LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) and a vLEI issued by GLEIF before joining a ceremony, so they legitimately represent their institution. On-chain verification path is planned.
ark.who_desc: Ark is a proposal — an architecture and a set of working components offered to the institutions, professionals, and developers who have to make sovereign digital identity real. Find the role that fits you.
ark.ext_desc: Browser extension that validates document signatures and CA trust in the page, surfaces a trust score, and connects to the Station for verification flows.
ark.ext_l2: Trust score surfaced in the browser
ark.ext_l4: Bridges browser pages to the Station
ark.xx_desc: Each jurisdiction can deploy its own sovereign CA with its own governance scheme and institutional shareholders.

desktop.hero_title: One desktop. Six modules. Zero strangers.
desktop.hero_lead: The Station is an Electron desktop application that bundles your identity vault, document signer, verifier, mesh node, proctoring engine, and browser bridge into a single auditable shell. Every sensitive operation — from biometric liveness to PDF signing — runs on your own hardware, on code anyone can read.
desktop.modules_desc: The Station is a composition of independent modules that share a single encrypted vault. Each module is opt-in. You can run the Station purely as a vault, purely as a verifier, or activate every module for a full sovereign-identity workstation.
desktop.vault_desc: Encrypted local key store. Ed25519 signing key + xsalsa20-poly1305 + scrypt key derivation. The private key never leaves the device — not even to the Attestto company.
desktop.signer_desc: Sign PDFs with your vault key. Produces W3C Verifiable Credentials embedded directly into the document metadata. Recognized natively by verify.attestto.com — no plugin, no Adobe, no cloud.
desktop.verifier_desc: Drop a PDF onto the Station, get a forensic report: signature integrity, certificate chain, document hash, tamper detection. Same engine that runs at verify.attestto.com — but offline.
desktop.verifier_l2: National PKI roots (CR PJ, PF, MICITT)
desktop.mesh_desc: Every Station can become a peer in the Attestto Mesh — an encrypted libp2p network for credential anchoring, trust mirroring, and redundant verification. Blind-courier: nodes can't read what they carry.
desktop.proctor_desc: White-box exam proctoring that runs entirely on the candidate's machine. Camera, screen, and process monitoring with zero cloud video upload. The "proctor" is auditable code, not a stranger watching a feed.
desktop.bridge_desc: The Station pairs with the Attestto ID extension via the open @attestto/id-wallet-adapter protocol. Web pages discover the wallet, request signatures, and receive credentials — without the Station ever exposing your private key to the page.
desktop.bridge_l2: DID login, document signing, credential push
desktop.electron_title: A browser engine with hardware access
desktop.electron_desc: Sovereign identity needs deep access to the device — camera, screen, processes, file system, smart cards — which a sandboxed web page cannot provide. Electron gives the Station the Chromium rendering engine for a modern UI and Node.js for direct hardware access. The result is a modular desktop that ships as a single installer and runs everywhere your team already works.
desktop.electron_card1_desc: The same rendering pipeline that powers verify.attestto.com runs the Station's UI. PDF preview, OCR, biometric overlays, signature stamps — all rendered with web technology you can inspect.
desktop.electron_card2_desc: Direct file system, process inspection, smart card interfaces, mesh networking, and OS-level keychain integration — capabilities a normal browser refuses to grant.
desktop.electron_card3_desc: The Station ships as a notarized DMG, MSI, and AppImage. Source code is open. Reproducible builds are on the roadmap so anyone can verify the binary matches the published commit.
desktop.trust_desc: A signature is only as trustworthy as the identity verification behind it. The Station surfaces an explicit trust tier on every credential it issues, so verifiers and counterparties know exactly what evidence the signer presented.
desktop.trust_aplus_desc: Costa Rica Firma Digital smart card (PKCS#11). Qualified electronic signature recognized under Ley 8454.
desktop.trust_a_desc: Cédula scan + Padrón Electoral + facial recognition + liveness proof + Firma Digital seal.
desktop.trust_b_desc: Cédula scan + Padrón Electoral cross-check + facial recognition + liveness proof. The default for citizen-issued credentials.
desktop.trust_c_desc: Cédula scanned and OCR'd, no Padrón cross-check, no biometrics. Useful for non-binding workflows.
desktop.trust_d_desc: Holder-asserted data with no external verification. Always labeled, never silently upgraded.
desktop.auditors_title: Read the code. Run the binary. File issues.
desktop.auditors_desc: Every claim on this page is backed by a public repository. If anything looks wrong, the right move is to open the source — not to take our word for it.
desktop.cta_title: Run sovereign identity on your own desktop
desktop.cta_desc: The Station is in early access for professionals, institutions, and auditors. Tell us who you are and what you would use it for, and we will get you a build that fits your jurisdiction.

dev.hero_title: The credential infrastructure layer. Fork it, extend it, ship it.
dev.hero_lead: Attestto is sovereign identity infrastructure. You build modules on top. Citizens use your module. You earn 60% of every transaction fee. The platform handles identity, verification, and distribution.
dev.start_desc: Pick your path based on what you need. Each leads to a different part of the stack.
dev.path1_title: I want to build a module for the Attestto App
dev.path1_desc: Start with @attestto/module-sdk. Your module runs inside the PWA. You get identity, vault, LLM, and distribution for free.
dev.path2_title: I need to verify Costa Rica documents
dev.path2_desc: Use @attestto/verify web component. Drop it in your page. Drag-and-drop PDF verification against BCCR PKI. Zero config.
dev.path3_title: I need to issue verifiable credentials
dev.path3_desc: Use cr-vc-sdk + cr-vc-schemas. Define your credential type, sign with your DID, deliver to wallets.
dev.path4_desc: Read the did:sns spec. Resolve decentralized identifiers via Solana Name Service. W3C standards-track.
dev.path5_title: I want to run a mesh node
dev.path5_desc: Download Station (desktop app) or run attestto-mesh directly. Relay verification proofs for the network and earn micropayments.
dev.arch_title: Three layers. Your module lives in the middle.
dev.arch_desc: The platform handles infrastructure (bottom) and user surfaces (top). You build modules that plug into both.
dev.sdk_title: Ship a module in a week
dev.sdk_desc: The SDK gives you identity, vault access, on-device LLM, credential gating, and distribution. You focus on your domain logic.
dev.step1_desc: Start from cr-driving as your reference. It implements every SDK interface with real logic you can study.
dev.step2_desc: Set your module ID, required credentials, capabilities, routes, and icon. The manifest tells the shell what your module needs and provides.
dev.step3_desc: The shell calls install(ctx) with a context object. You get credential access, storage, LLM, biometric auth, navigation, and inbox push.
dev.step4_desc: Vue 3 components, lazy-loaded via your manifest routes. The shell handles auth, navigation chrome, and credential gating.
dev.step5_desc: Optional: return an OnboardingFlow with contextual LLM prompts. Add proctored exams with mastery tracking and VC issuance on completion.
dev.step6_desc: Open a PR to the module registry. Community testers validate. Once merged, your module is available to every Attestto user.
dev.ctx_identity_desc: User's DID, credential vault, WebAuthn biometric auth. You never manage keys.
dev.ctx_creds_desc: Read from vault, write to vault, gate access by credential type. W3C Verifiable Credentials.
dev.ctx_llm_desc: Gemma 2B runs locally via WebGPU. Contextual help, Q&A, document analysis. No data leaves the device.
dev.ctx_storage_desc: Namespaced key-value store. Your data is isolated from other modules. Persists across sessions.
dev.ctx_inbox_desc: Push notifications, action items, and warnings to the user's home screen. Priority-sorted.
dev.ctx_dist_desc: Your module is available to every Attestto user. PWA on mobile, Station on desktop. No app store needed.
dev.bounty_desc: Each card is a real problem affecting real people. Full specs are written. You build the module, you earn 60% of transaction fees. Forever.
dev.bounty_cta: Full specs and reference implementation on GitHub
dev.econ_title: You earn 60% of every transaction. Forever.
dev.econ_desc: No upfront cost. No subscription. Build a module, submit it, and earn a majority share of every transaction fee your module generates.
dev.econ_example_desc: 8,000 notaries, ~20 filings/month, $2 per filing = $320K/month gross. Your 60% = $192K/month. That's the addressable market for a single Costa Rica module.
dev.econ_sponsor_desc: When an institution sponsors your module (e.g., a bank sponsors FinancialInclusion), the split adjusts: 50% Attestto / 35% sponsor / 10% testers / 5% open. You negotiate directly with the sponsor.
dev.qs_title: From zero to module in 5 minutes

modules.label: Modules
modules.hero_title: Install what you need. Nothing more.
modules.hero_lead: Each module adds a specific credential capability to your Attestto wallet. Self-sovereign, on-device, open source.
modules.identity_desc: Scan your cedula, driver's license, or passport. Create verifiable credentials signed with your own key.
modules.driving_desc: Theory exam prep, mastery tracking, and digital driving license credentials aligned with COSEVI/DGEV.
modules.signing_desc: AI-powered document analysis, flagged clauses, guided Q&A — then sign with your Ed25519 key.
modules.build_desc: The module SDK is open source. Anyone can create a module that issues, verifies, or manages credentials. 60% of revenue goes to the builder.

mod_identity.label: Identity Module
mod_identity.hero_title: Your identity, your device, your keys.
mod_identity.hero_lead: Scan your cedula, driver's license, or passport. The OCR runs on your phone — no images are uploaded. Sign the extracted data with your Ed25519 key to create a verifiable credential.
mod_identity.how_title: Three steps to a digital credential
mod_identity.step1_desc: Use your phone camera to capture the front and back of your document. The MRZ (machine-readable zone) is extracted via on-device OCR.
mod_identity.step2_desc: Verify the extracted data. Correct any OCR errors. The confidence score tells you how reliable the extraction was.
mod_identity.step3_desc: Your Ed25519 key signs the credential with biometric confirmation. The verifiable credential is stored in your encrypted vault.
mod_identity.cedula_desc: Costa Rica national ID card. TD1 MRZ on the back. Extracts cedula number, full name, date of birth, expiry, nationality, and sex.
mod_identity.license_desc: Costa Rica driver's license. TD1 MRZ on the back + category table on the front. Extracts categories (A1-E3), validity dates, points, and restrictions.
mod_identity.passport_desc: Any ICAO 9303-compliant passport (TD3 MRZ). Extracts document number, names, date of birth, expiry, nationality, and issuing country.
mod_identity.priv1: OCR runs in-browser via Tesseract.js WebAssembly
mod_identity.priv2: Photos are processed locally and never uploaded
mod_identity.priv3: Private key stored in IndexedDB, gated behind WebAuthn biometrics
mod_identity.priv4: Credentials encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM
mod_identity.priv5: SD-JWT selective disclosure — share only the fields you choose
mod_identity.priv8: Open source — audit the code yourself
mod_identity.cta_desc: Free, open source, no sign-up. Open the app on your phone and scan your first document.

mod_driving.label: Driving Module
mod_driving.hero_title: Prove your competency, not just your score.
mod_driving.hero_lead: Study for the COSEVI theory exam with spaced repetition. Track your mastery over time. Every exam session is cryptographically sealed and signed with your key.
mod_driving.feat1_desc: Questions adapt to your performance. Topics you struggle with appear more often. The algorithm optimizes long-term retention, not cramming.
mod_driving.feat2_desc: Your competency score decays over time — faster at novice level, slower at expert. This reflects real-world knowledge loss and encourages continuous review.
mod_driving.feat3_desc: Full exam sessions with SHA-256 hash chain integrity. Every answer is cryptographically linked. The sealed session becomes a verifiable credential.
mod_driving.cred1_desc: Issued after completing a proctored exam session. Includes score, category, number of questions, exam session ID, and the integrity hash chain.
mod_driving.cred2_desc: Mastery credential proving sustained competency. Includes competency level, exams passed, mastery score, and renewal date based on decay rate.
mod_driving.cta_desc: Free, open source, works offline. Install the app as a PWA and start your first practice session.

mod_signing.label: Signing Module
mod_signing.hero_lead: Upload a document. On-device AI analyzes it, flags risky clauses, and asks you the right questions. When you're ready, sign with your Ed25519 key.
mod_signing.how_title: Four steps to an informed signature
mod_signing.step1_desc: Upload a PDF. The document stays on your device.
mod_signing.step2_desc: Gemma 2B analyzes clauses, categorizes the document, and flags risks.
mod_signing.step3_desc: Answer guided questions about the flagged sections. The AI recommends an action.
mod_signing.step4_desc: Ed25519 signature with biometric confirmation. Audit trail PDF generated.
mod_signing.out1_desc: The original PDF with an Attestto signature embedded in the metadata and a visible stamp on the last page. Verifiable at verify.attestto.com.
mod_signing.out2_desc: A verifiable credential in your wallet recording what you signed, the document hash, risk assessment, and your answers. Proves informed consent.
mod_signing.ai_title: No cloud. No data collection. No compromise.
mod_signing.ai_desc: The AI model (Google Gemma 2B) runs entirely in your browser using WebGPU. Downloaded once, cached locally. Your documents never leave your device. Even the AI's analysis stays on your phone.
mod_signing.cta_desc: Free, open source, no sign-up. Open the app, upload a PDF, and let the AI help you understand it.
